words.enDefinition: A recognised origin or form of legal rules, such as legislation or judicial precedent in a particular system.

examples.en: The lecturer asks which source of law supports the rule printed on the first page of the handout.
examples.zh: 老师询问讲义第一页所印规则依据的是哪一种「法源」。

examples.en: The table identifies a source of law for each proposition raised in the fictional seminar problem.
examples.zh: 这张表为虚构研讨题提出的每项命题列出一个「法源」。

words.enDefinition: The ordering of legal norms by authority within a legal system, relevant when rules conflict.

examples.en: Our seminar uses a diagram of the hierarchy of norms to compare national and local legal provisions.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「法律规范位阶」示意图比较国家和地方的法律条文。

examples.en: The fictional example asks where a regulation belongs in the hierarchy of norms shown on the board.
examples.zh: 虚构示例询问，一项规章在黑板所示的「法律规范位阶」中位于哪里。

collocations: position in the hierarchy of norms

words.enDefinition: A particular rule or clause forming part of a written constitution.

examples.en: The mock judgment starts with the constitutional provision quoted near the beginning of the course handout.
examples.zh: 模拟判决先讨论课程讲义开头附近引用的「宪法条款」。

examples.en: Our worksheet separates the text of the constitutional provision from the professor's explanatory notes beside it.
examples.zh: 练习单把「宪法条款」正文与教授写在旁边的注释分开。

words.enDefinition: The governing constitutional text of a state in a federation, such as a US state.

examples.en: The American law seminar presents a state constitution alongside the federal Constitution for a comparison exercise.
examples.zh: 美国法律研讨课把一部「州宪法」和联邦宪法并列展示，作为比较练习。

examples.en: In the fictional state dispute, the question turns on which provision of the state constitution applies.
examples.zh: 在虚构的州法争议中，问题取决于「州宪法」的哪一条适用。

words.enDefinition: A law enacted by the national legislature of a federation, such as the US Congress.

examples.en: The classroom example asks readers to locate the federal statute cited in the fictional agency notice.
examples.zh: 课堂示例要求读者找出虚构机构通知所引用的「联邦制定法」。

examples.en: The textbook uses a fictional federal statute to illustrate how Congress sets out duties in legislation.
examples.zh: 教材用一部虚构「联邦制定法」说明美国国会如何在立法中列明义务。

words.enDefinition: A law enacted by a state legislature within a federation, as distinct from national legislation.

examples.en: Our American legal research exercise asks which state statute the fictional judgment applies to the dispute.
examples.zh: 美国法律检索练习要求判断虚构判决在争议中适用的是哪一部「州制定法」。

examples.en: Students compared the definition in the proposed state statute with the wording of the assigned federal law.
examples.zh: 学生把拟议「州制定法」的定义与指定阅读的联邦法措辞作比较。

words.enDefinition: In the UK, legislation made when a bill has passed the required parliamentary stages and received Royal Assent.

examples.en: The handout uses a fictional Act of Parliament to show where its long title would appear.
examples.zh: 讲义用一部虚构「议会制定法」说明其长标题通常出现在何处。

examples.en: In the seminar, students separate the Act of Parliament from regulations made under its authority.
examples.zh: 在研讨课上，学生把「议会制定法」与依据其授权制定的规章区分开。

collocations: provisions of an Act of Parliament

words.enDefinition: Legislation enacted directly by a legislature, such as Acts of Parliament in the UK.

examples.en: The UK law worksheet asks us to label each document as primary legislation or another type of source.
examples.zh: 英国法律练习单要求我们标明每份文件属于「主要立法」还是其他类型的法源。

examples.en: Our class checks which part of the primary legislation provided authority for the fictional regulation.
examples.zh: 全班核对属于「主要立法」的文件中，哪一部分给虚构规章提供了授权。

words.enDefinition: Legally binding rules made by a person or body exercising rulemaking power delegated by primary legislation.

examples.en: The British textbook introduces secondary legislation alongside an extract showing who may make the authorised rules.
examples.zh: 英国教材在介绍「次级立法」时，附上一段说明哪些主体获准制定规则的摘录。

examples.en: The seminar compares two pieces of secondary legislation made under different sections of the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较了依据虚构议会法案不同条款制定的两部「次级立法」。

words.enDefinition: A common form of UK secondary legislation made under an authority granted by an Act.

examples.en: The tutor asked us to locate the enabling Act listed at the start of the sample statutory instrument.
examples.zh: 老师要求我们找出「法定文书」样本开头列出的授权法。

examples.en: The notes explain why the fictional statutory instrument and its enabling Act have different publication references.
examples.zh: 笔记解释虚构「法定文书」和授权法为什么各有不同的出版编号。

words.enDefinition: An Act that grants an authority the power to make further legal rules or instruments.

examples.en: We checked the enabling Act to see which body the fictional statutory instrument named as its maker.
examples.zh: 我们核对「授权制定规则的法令」，查明虚构法定文书所列的制定主体。

examples.en: The lecture puts the enabling Act beside the regulations so students can follow the chain of authority.
examples.zh: 讲座把「授权制定规则的法令」和规章并排展示，让学生看清权力的来源。

collocations: relevant provision in an enabling Act

words.enDefinition: A provision that grants particular legal powers, such as the power to make regulations.

examples.en: The UK law exercise asks which enabling provision authorises publication of the fictional instrument under study.
examples.zh: 英国法律练习询问，哪项「授权性条款」准许发布正在学习的虚构文书。

examples.en: We drew a line from the enabling provision to the regulation it authorises in the classroom outline.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂提纲里，从「授权性条款」画一条线连到它授权制定的规章。

collocations: authority conferred by an enabling provision

words.enDefinition: A power conferred by one authority on another to perform a specified function, such as making rules.

examples.en: The UK seminar asks how the delegated power is described in the relevant section of the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 英国法律研讨课询问，虚构法案的相关条文怎样描述「授予下级主体的权力」。

examples.en: Our notes identify which organisation exercises the delegated power and which legislature establishes its limits.
examples.zh: 笔记指出哪个机构行使「授予下级主体的权力」，以及哪个立法机关规定其限度。

words.enDefinition: A power in UK primary legislation to amend or repeal provisions of primary legislation by secondary legislation.

examples.en: The parliamentary reading compares a Henry VIII power with a narrower power to make administrative rules.
examples.zh: 议会制度读物把「亨利八世权力」与范围更窄的制定行政规则权力作比较。

examples.en: The fictional bill contains a Henry VIII power whose scope the class examines in the following section.
examples.zh: 虚构议案含有一项「亨利八世权力」，全班在下一节课研究其范围。

collocations: scope of a Henry VIII power

words.enDefinition: Beyond the legal powers given to a person or body, often used when reviewing the validity of an act or rule.

examples.en: The mock judgment asks whether the fictional regulation was ultra vires under the authority granted by Parliament.
examples.zh: 模拟判决讨论，依议会所授予的权限，虚构规章是否是「超越权限的」。

examples.en: In class, we compared the grant of power with the conduct alleged to be ultra vires.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把授予的权力与被指为「超越权限的」行为作比较。

words.enDefinition: Within the legal powers given to a person or body in the circumstances.

examples.en: The mock judgment explains why the fictional authority's decision was intra vires under the relevant legislative provision.
examples.zh: 模拟判决解释了依相关法律条文，虚构机关的决定为何是「在权限以内的」。

examples.en: Our exercise asks what language in the enabling Act supports calling the rule intra vires.
examples.zh: 练习询问，授权法中的哪些文字支持把这项规则认定为「在权限以内的」。

words.enDefinition: Legal power to make or enact rules of a specified kind, as conferred under a particular system.

examples.en: The constitutional diagram identifies which body has legislative authority over the subject in our fictional exercise.
examples.zh: 宪法示意图指出，在虚构练习中哪个机构对这个事项享有「立法权限」。

examples.en: Our model answer cites the constitutional provision that establishes legislative authority for the fictional national legislature.
examples.zh: 参考答案引用了确立虚构国家立法机关「立法权限」的宪法条款。

words.enDefinition: The process through which a public agency makes, changes, or repeals regulations using its legal authority.

examples.en: The American law handout introduces agency rulemaking through a fictional proposal about the format of public reports.
examples.zh: 美国法律讲义通过一项关于公共报告格式的虚构提案介绍「行政机构制定规则」。

examples.en: We used a timeline to distinguish agency rulemaking from the earlier process of passing the enabling law.
examples.zh: 我们用时间线把「行政机构制定规则」与更早通过授权法的过程区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A public US agency notice describing proposed rulemaking and providing relevant information about participation when notice-and-comment procedure applies.

examples.en: The American exercise asks students to identify the notice of proposed rulemaking on a fictional Federal Register page.
examples.zh: 美国练习要求学生在一页虚构的《联邦公报》上找出「拟议规则制定公告」。

examples.en: The notice of proposed rulemaking lists the authority cited by the agency in our sample document.
examples.zh: 在样本文书中，「拟议规则制定公告」列出了该机构援引的权限依据。

collocations: publish a notice of proposed rulemaking
comment on a notice of proposed rulemaking
contents of a notice of proposed rulemaking

words.enDefinition: The period during which a public body accepts comments from the public on a proposal, such as a proposed regulation.

examples.en: The fictional agency notice specifies a public comment period on the first page of the reading packet.
examples.zh: 虚构机构公报在阅读资料第一页规定了「公开意见征询期」。

examples.en: The rulemaking timeline shows where the public comment period falls between publication of the proposal and agency review.
examples.zh: 制定规则的时间线显示，「公开意见征询期」处于发布提案和机构审查之间的什么位置。

words.enDefinition: In US agency rulemaking, a regulation issued in final form, often with a stated effective date.

examples.en: The classroom exercise asks when the fictional final rule was published and when it would take effect.
examples.zh: 课堂练习询问虚构「正式规则」在何时公布、何时生效。

examples.en: Our sample final rule lists the sections of the federal regulations that the issuing agency will amend.
examples.zh: 「正式规则」样本列出了发布机构将要修改的联邦法规条款。

collocations: effective date of a final rule

words.enDefinition: The official US federal publication for documents such as agency rules, proposed rules, and notices.

examples.en: We searched a sample Federal Register issue for the date printed next to the fictional agency rule.
examples.zh: 我们在一期「《联邦公报》」样刊中寻找印在虚构机构规则旁边的日期。

examples.en: Our professor explained why a Federal Register citation sometimes appears next to a codified regulation's text.
examples.zh: 教授解释，为什么法规汇编条文的旁边有时会出现「《联邦公报》」引文。

words.enDefinition: The codification of generally applicable and permanent rules published by US federal departments and agencies.

examples.en: The American law handout shows how the Code of Federal Regulations arranges agency rules by subject.
examples.zh: 美国法律讲义展示了「《美国联邦法规汇编》」如何按主题编排各机构制定的规则。

examples.en: We located the title number in the sample Code of Federal Regulations citation before reading the section.
examples.zh: 阅读该节法规以前，我们先在「《美国联邦法规汇编》」的引文样本中找出编号。

collocations: title of the Code of Federal Regulations
section of the Code of Federal Regulations
codified in the Code of Federal Regulations

words.enDefinition: A regularly updated online editorial compilation of US federal regulations, distinct from the official legal edition of the CFR.

examples.en: The librarian shows how the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations labels the date of the displayed version.
examples.zh: 图书馆员演示「《美国联邦法规汇编》电子版」怎样标明所显示版本的日期。

examples.en: Our notes list the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations beside the annually updated printed version for comparison.
examples.zh: 笔记把「《美国联邦法规汇编》电子版」和每年更新的印刷版本并列，供我们比较。

collocations: search the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
consult the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
version in the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations

words.enDefinition: A subject-based codification of the general and permanent federal laws of the United States.

examples.en: The library worksheet distinguishes the United States Code from the chronological collection used in the next question.
examples.zh: 图书馆练习单区分了「《美国法典》」与下一题使用的按时间顺序编纂的汇编。

examples.en: Our seminar locates a definition in the United States Code using the title and section supplied in class.
examples.zh: 研讨课根据课上提供的编号和条号，在「《美国法典》」中找出一项定义。

collocations: section of the United States Code
title of the United States Code
codified in the United States Code

words.enDefinition: The official chronological collection in which US public laws, private laws, and certain other documents are published.

examples.en: The American seminar uses the United States Statutes at Large to discuss how enacted laws are arranged chronologically.
examples.zh: 美国法律研讨课用「《美国联邦法令全书》」说明已制定的法律怎样按时间顺序编排。

examples.en: We identified the volume number in the United States Statutes at Large reference on our reading worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们在阅读练习单的「《美国联邦法令全书》」引文中找出了卷号。

collocations: volume of the United States Statutes at Large
citation to the United States Statutes at Large
published in the United States Statutes at Large

words.enDefinition: A number identifying an enacted US federal public law by Congress and its sequence within that Congress.

examples.en: The library instructor asks us to locate the public law number on a sample American legislative document.
examples.zh: 图书馆讲师要求我们在一份美国立法文书样本上找出「美国联邦公法编号」。

examples.en: The public law number and the code citation appear in different places on the classroom reference card.
examples.zh: 课堂参考卡上的「美国联邦公法编号」和法典引文出现在不同位置。

words.enDefinition: In US federal publication, an individual publication of an enacted law before compilation in the Statutes at Large.

examples.en: The handout reproduces the front page of a slip law to show how headings appear in that format.
examples.zh: 讲义复制了「单行法印本」的首页，说明标题在这种格式里怎样呈现。

examples.en: Students matched a sample slip law to its later entry in the chronological collection of federal laws.
examples.zh: 学生们将一份「单行法印本」样本与它后来在按时间汇编的联邦法令全书中的条目配对。

collocations: publish an Act as a slip law

words.enDefinition: A title of the United States Code enacted as a statutory text by Congress.

examples.en: The American law handout explains how to tell whether a title is a positive law title.
examples.zh: 美国法讲义解释了如何判断《美国法典》的一编是否属于「经立法通过的法典编」。

examples.en: The table marks the assigned positive law title so students can discuss its status as statutory text.
examples.zh: 表格标出指定阅读的「经立法通过的法典编」，供学生讨论它作为成文法文本的地位。

collocations: text of a positive law title

words.enDefinition: A UK parliamentary procedure under which a statutory instrument requires express approval in the required house or houses.

examples.en: The parliamentary worksheet compares the affirmative resolution procedure with another process used for some statutory instruments.
examples.zh: 议会制度练习单将「肯定决议程序」与某些法定文书适用的另一种程序作比较。

examples.en: Our example asks which house must approve the instrument under the stated affirmative resolution procedure.
examples.zh: 示例询问，按照所述「肯定决议程序」，议会哪一院必须批准这项法定文书。

collocations: subject to the affirmative resolution procedure
instrument under the affirmative resolution procedure

words.enDefinition: A UK parliamentary procedure allowing a statutory instrument to stand unless annulled under the applicable procedure.

examples.en: Our UK legislative diagram labels the negative resolution procedure on a branch separate from express approval.
examples.zh: 我们绘制的英国立法流程图把「否定决议程序」标在与明示批准不同的分支上。

examples.en: The textbook asks when the negative resolution procedure applies to the fictional transport instrument in the attachment.
examples.zh: 教材追问附件中虚构的交通法定文书何时适用「否定决议程序」。

collocations: subject to the negative resolution procedure
instrument under the negative resolution procedure

words.enDefinition: Formal approval by the monarch that completes the process by which a UK parliamentary bill becomes an Act.

examples.en: The UK timeline places Royal Assent after the parliamentary stages and before the Act's separate commencement date.
examples.zh: 英国时间线把「御准」放在议会各阶段之后、法令另定的生效日期之前。

examples.en: Our textbook uses a fictional Act to illustrate where the date of Royal Assent is recorded.
examples.zh: 教材用一部虚构法令展示了「御准」日期记录在什么位置。

words.enDefinition: A UK constitutional principle concerning Parliament's supreme lawmaking authority within the constitutional system.

examples.en: The first UK constitutional law class introduces parliamentary sovereignty before discussing how courts interpret Acts of Parliament.
examples.zh: 英国宪法第一堂课先介绍「议会主权」，再讨论法院如何解释议会制定法。

examples.en: The summary on parliamentary sovereignty asks students to identify which institution makes primary legislation in the example.
examples.zh: 关于「议会主权」的摘要要求学生指出示例中哪个机构制定主要立法。

words.enDefinition: The formal abbreviated name of an Act or other legislative instrument, used to identify or cite it.

examples.en: The UK exercise asks us to use the short title when referring to the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 英国练习要求我们在提及这部虚构法令时使用「法令简称」。

examples.en: Students found the short title in one section and the more descriptive wording at the top.
examples.zh: 学生们在一项条文里找出「法令简称」，并在文件上方发现了更详细的表述。

words.enDefinition: A formal descriptive title indicating the subject or purposes of an Act, particularly in UK legislation.

examples.en: Our exercise asks readers to compare the long title with the provisions of the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 练习要求读者将「法令长标题」与虚构法令的条款作比较。

examples.en: The long title on the sample Act describes its subject without listing every section in detail.
examples.zh: 样本法令上的「法令长标题」说明了法令主题，无须逐条详述。

words.enDefinition: A conventional statement identifying the lawmaking authority and formally introducing the enacted provisions.

examples.en: The handout prints an enacting formula above the first section of the fictional Act for discussion.
examples.zh: 讲义将「法令制定语」印在虚构法令第一条上方，供全班讨论。

examples.en: We compared the enacting formula in the sample with the headings that organise the substantive provisions.
examples.zh: 我们把样本里的「法令制定语」与编排实体条款的标题作比较。

words.enDefinition: An individual text unit within a statute that sets out a legal rule, power, definition, or related matter.

examples.en: The mock judgment quotes a statutory provision before explaining how its conditions relate to the fictional dispute.
examples.zh: 模拟判决先引用一项「制定法条款」，再解释其条件与虚构争议有何关系。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks us to locate the statutory provision making the requirement in the reading binding.
examples.zh: 练习单要求找出赋予读物中的该项要求以约束力的「制定法条款」。

words.enDefinition: A provision that states a rule, right, obligation, or other substantive legal effect.

examples.en: The tutor asked which operative provision establishes the obligation mentioned in the sample Act's descriptive introduction.
examples.zh: 老师询问，样本法令的说明性引言提到的义务由哪一项「规定法律效果的条款」确立。

examples.en: We highlighted the operative provision governing the fictional case before reading the neighbouring definitions and notes.
examples.zh: 阅读相邻的定义和注释以前，我们标出了适用于虚构案例的「规定法律效果的条款」。

words.enDefinition: In statutes using this heading, the section that defines terms or sets out rules for reading the Act.

examples.en: The legislation worksheet asks students to find the interpretation section before deciding what the defined term means.
examples.zh: 立法阅读练习单要求学生找出「释义条文」，再判断已定义术语的含义。

examples.en: Under the interpretation section of the fictional Act, the definition applies throughout the document unless otherwise stated.
examples.zh: 根据虚构法令的「释义条文」，除非另有说明，该定义适用于整部文件。

words.zhGloss: 制定法中的已定义术语
words.enDefinition: A word or phrase given a specified meaning by a statute for use within its stated scope.
acceptedZhAnswers: 制定法中的已定义术语

examples.en: In the fictional extract, a defined term in a statute has a narrower meaning than everyday usage.
examples.zh: 在虚构摘录中，一个「制定法中的已定义术语」含义比日常用法更窄。

examples.en: The exercise traces a defined term in a statute back to the section giving its special meaning.
examples.zh: 练习把一个「制定法中的已定义术语」追溯到给出其特定含义的条文。

collocations: locate a defined term in a statute
scope of a defined term in a statute
use of a defined term in a statute

words.zhGloss: 对另一条文的交叉引用
words.enDefinition: A reference directing the reader to another numbered section for a relevant definition, condition, or rule.
acceptedZhAnswers: 对另一条文的交叉引用

examples.en: The text uses a cross-reference to another section where the scope of the exception is set out.
examples.zh: 正文用「对另一条文的交叉引用」指向说明该例外范围的位置。

examples.en: We followed the cross-reference to another section and read the definition in its original statutory wording.
examples.zh: 我们沿着「对另一条文的交叉引用」找过去，阅读了定义在法令中的原文。

collocations: follow a cross-reference to another section
check a cross-reference to another section
insert a cross-reference to another section

words.enDefinition: A numbered or titled part attached to legislation that sets out supplementary or detailed statutory material.

examples.en: The fictional Act sends readers to a statutory schedule for the full list of covered properties.
examples.zh: 虚构法令让读者查阅「法令附表」，获取所涵盖财产的完整列表。

examples.en: Students checked whether the table in the statutory schedule was part of the legislation itself.
examples.zh: 学生核对「法令附表」中的表格是否属于立法文本本身。

collocations: list items in a statutory schedule

words.expression: explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument
words.lemma: explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument
words.enDefinition: A document accompanying UK secondary legislation to explain its purpose, policy background, and practical effect to Parliament and other readers.
acceptedEnVariants: explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument

examples.en: The handout includes an explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument alongside the text of the fictional instrument.
examples.zh: 讲义将一份「法定文书说明备忘录」与虚构法定文书正文并列收录。

examples.en: We read the explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument before summarising its policy background for class.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读「法定文书说明备忘录」，然后在课上概述其政策背景。

collocations: prepare an explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument
consult an explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument
publish an explanatory memorandum to a statutory instrument

words.enDefinition: Separate material prepared to explain the context or operation of legislation, distinguished from the enacted provisions themselves.

examples.en: The UK law handout places explanatory notes to legislation beside the fictional section they discuss in class.
examples.zh: 英国法律讲义把「立法说明」和课堂所讨论的虚构条文并排放置。

examples.en: We compared the explanatory notes to legislation with the text actually enacted by the fictional legislature.
examples.zh: 我们把「立法说明」与虚构立法机关正式通过的法条文本作了比较。

collocations: legal status of explanatory notes to legislation

words.enDefinition: In UK legislative drafting, the jurisdiction or jurisdictions of whose law a provision forms part.

examples.en: The UK exercise asks us to trace territorial extent using the final provisions of the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 英国练习要求我们根据虚构法令的最后几条查明「条文归属的法域范围」。

examples.en: On the worksheet, territorial extent is shown separately from the date the rule comes into force.
examples.zh: 练习单分别列出「条文归属的法域范围」和规则生效之日。

words.zhGloss: 法律在地域上的实际适用
words.enDefinition: In UK legislation, the places or geographic connections in relation to which a provision operates in practice.
acceptedZhAnswers: 法律在地域上的实际适用

examples.en: Our example distinguishes territorial application from the legal systems of which the fictional provision forms part.
examples.zh: 示例将「法律在地域上的实际适用」与虚构条文归属哪些法律体系区分开来。

examples.en: The section on territorial application states which places the rule concerns in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，关于「法律在地域上的实际适用」的条文指明这一规则涉及哪些地区。

words.enDefinition: A provision that states or determines when some or all of an enactment comes into force.

examples.en: In the fictional Act, a commencement provision gives different start dates for two groups of sections.
examples.zh: 在虚构法令中，一项「生效条款」为两组条文规定了不同的起始日期。

examples.en: We read the commencement provision before deciding which version applied on the date in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在判断练习所列日期适用哪个版本以前，我们先阅读了「生效条款」。

words.enDefinition: A UK legal instrument made under statutory power to bring provisions of legislation into force.

examples.en: The tutor used a fictional commencement order to explain why some provisions take effect later than others.
examples.zh: 老师用一份虚构「生效令」解释为什么有些条文比其他条文晚生效。

examples.en: We matched the commencement order to the section that authorised it in the classroom materials.
examples.zh: 我们把课堂材料里的「生效令」与授权制定它的条文对应起来。

collocations: come into force under a commencement order
date specified in a commencement order

words.enDefinition: A rule treating legislation as having come into force at a stated time for legal purposes.

examples.en: The exercise compares the publication date with the date of deemed commencement in the fictional legislation.
examples.zh: 练习比较了虚构立法的公布日期与「视为生效」日期。

examples.en: Our notes explain how deemed commencement affects the date used in the imaginary timeline under discussion.
examples.zh: 笔记说明「视为生效」如何影响正在讨论的虚构时间线所采用的日期。

words.enDefinition: To start having legal effect, when said of legislation or a particular provision.

examples.en: The fictional order states when three sections come into force and leaves the other dates for later.
examples.zh: 虚构命令列出三项条文何时「开始生效」，其余日期留待以后确定。

examples.en: Our reading exercise asks whether both provisions come into force on the same date under the sample Act.
examples.zh: 阅读练习询问，按照样本法令，两项条文是否在同一天「开始生效」。

collocations: come into force on a specified date

words.expression: in force on a given date
words.lemma: in force on a given date
words.enDefinition: Legally operative on a particular date, taking account of the relevant commencement, amendment, or repeal provisions.
acceptedEnVariants: in force on a given date

examples.en: The worksheet asks which subsection was in force on a given date in the fictional timeline.
examples.zh: 练习单要求找出虚构时间线上哪一个分条「在指定日期有效」。

examples.en: The tutor compared published versions to show how to check wording in force on a given date.
examples.zh: 老师通过比较已公布的版本，演示如何核查「在指定日期有效」的条文措辞。

collocations: text in force on a given date
provision in force on a given date
verify what was in force on a given date

words.enDefinition: A provision explaining how legal rules apply during the change from one legal regime to another.

examples.en: The textbook uses a transitional provision to show how the fictional statute treats matters already in progress.
examples.zh: 教材用一项「过渡条款」说明虚构制定法如何处理已经开始的事项。

examples.en: The class read the transitional provision after comparing the commencement dates printed on the two handouts.
examples.zh: 全班比较两份讲义印出的生效日期后，阅读了「过渡条款」。

words.enDefinition: A provision preserving an existing right, obligation, rule, or pending matter despite legislative change.

examples.en: Our example uses a saving provision to preserve earlier rights when the fictional statute replaces an older rule.
examples.zh: 示例用一项「保留条款」说明虚构制定法取代旧规则时如何保留先前产生的权利。

examples.en: The exercise asks which earlier obligations survive because of the saving provision quoted in the imaginary judgment.
examples.zh: 练习追问，虚构判决引用的「保留条款」使哪些先前义务继续存在。

words.enDefinition: A legislative provision causing a rule or power to expire at a set time unless it is renewed or extended as allowed.

examples.en: The fictional statute's sunset clause links the expiration of a temporary power to a date in the schedule.
examples.zh: 虚构制定法的「自动失效条款」把一项临时权力的终止与附表中的日期关联起来。

examples.en: We checked whether the sunset clause applied to the entire fictional Act or only selected provisions.
examples.zh: 我们核对「自动失效条款」适用于整部虚构法令还是只适用于特定条文。

collocations: extend the deadline under a sunset clause

words.enDefinition: To remove a statutory provision's legal force through another enactment or recognised legislative act.

examples.en: The fictional legislature voted to repeal a statutory provision that had appeared in the old chapter.
examples.zh: 虚构立法机关投票决定「废止制定法条款」，这项条款原见于旧的一章。

examples.en: The outline asks which part of the new Act would repeal a statutory provision cited in the exercise.
examples.zh: 提纲询问，新法令的哪个部分将「废止制定法条款」，所指是练习引用的那一条。

collocations: vote to repeal a statutory provision
enact legislation to repeal a statutory provision

words.enDefinition: Repeal accomplished by language that states which legislation or provisions are being removed.

examples.en: The example of express repeal names the older sections directly in the text of the fictional Act.
examples.zh: 「明文废止」示例在虚构法令正文中直接点明了旧条文。

examples.en: The worksheet asks us to find express repeal in the schedule listing the changes to legislation.
examples.zh: 练习单要求我们在列明立法变动的附表中找出「明文废止」的内容。

words.enDefinition: Under certain legal systems, the displacement of an earlier rule by a later irreconcilable provision even without express repeal.

examples.en: Our comparative law exercise treats implied repeal as a separate question from what the new statute explicitly removes.
examples.zh: 比较法练习把「默示废止」与新制定法明确删除什么的问题分开讨论。

examples.en: The fictional judgment analyses implied repeal after trying to read the two statutory provisions together.
examples.zh: 虚构判决先尝试把两项制定法条款结合起来理解，再分析「默示废止」。

words.enDefinition: A legal change to the text or effect of an existing Act through a further legislative provision.

examples.en: The guide traces the amendment to an Act back to its source in the fictional legislative timeline.
examples.zh: 指南按虚构立法时间线，追溯了「对法令的修订」的法源。

examples.en: Our group compared the original wording with the amendment to an Act printed beside it in the handout.
examples.zh: 小组将原措辞与讲义旁边印出的「对法令的修订」作了比较。

collocations: enact an amendment to an Act
read an amendment to an Act
text of an amendment to an Act

words.enDefinition: A change to another provision or law needed to accommodate or maintain consistency with a principal legislative change.

examples.en: The sample statute lists a consequential amendment replacing an outdated reference introduced by an earlier Act.
examples.zh: 制定法样本列出一处「相应修订」，替换早期法令引入的一项过时引用。

examples.en: We identified the consequential amendment by reading the schedule alongside the main provision in the fictional bill.
examples.zh: 我们将附表与虚构议案的主要条文对照阅读，找出了「相应修订」。

words.enDefinition: An Act bringing existing statutory provisions on a subject together into a single legislative text.

examples.en: The tutor assigned a fictional consolidating Act to show how provisions from several earlier laws could be collected.
examples.zh: 老师指定阅读一部虚构「汇整法令」，说明如何汇集早先多部法律的条款。

examples.en: Our legal history exercise traces three provisions back to their sources before they appeared in the consolidating Act.
examples.zh: 法律史练习追溯了三项条文被收入「汇整法令」之前的来源。

collocations: consolidate legislation in a consolidating Act

words.enDefinition: In a legislative database, as the text stood when the legislation was originally enacted.

examples.en: The reading task asks for the text as enacted before considering amendments made over the following decade.
examples.zh: 阅读任务要求先找出「按最初制定文本」公布的版本，再考虑其后十年的修订。

examples.en: We selected the version as enacted to check the original wording used in the classroom comparison.
examples.zh: 我们选择了「按最初制定文本」显示的版本，核查课堂对比所用的原始措辞。

words.enDefinition: In UK legislative databases, in the form originally made, typically referring to a statutory instrument.

examples.en: The classroom exercise asks us to find the instrument as made before opening its revised text.
examples.zh: 课堂练习要求我们先找到法定文书「按最初制订文本」显示的版本，再打开修订文本。

examples.en: The notes mark the regulation as made because later amendments are discussed in a separate section.
examples.zh: 笔记标明这份规章是「按最初制订文本」展示的，因为后续修订另有专节讨论。

words.enDefinition: In a UK legislative database, a text updated editorially to show amendments and other applied effects, subject to update coverage.

examples.en: The website guide tells us how revised legislation displays a change beside the relevant fictional provision.
examples.zh: 网站指南告诉我们，「编入变动的立法文本」怎样在相关虚构条文旁显示一处修改。

examples.en: We compared revised legislation with the original instrument before deciding which version to quote in class.
examples.zh: 我们将「编入变动的立法文本」与原始法定文书作了比较，再决定在课上引用哪个版本。

words.enDefinition: A displayed version of legislation representing its text at a specified date, subject to the source's update coverage.

examples.en: The research worksheet asks for the point-in-time version corresponding to the date of the fictional events.
examples.zh: 检索练习单要求查找与虚构事件日期相符的「特定日期版本」。

examples.en: Our librarian shows how a point-in-time version can differ from the latest text displayed in the database.
examples.zh: 图书馆员演示「特定日期版本」可能与数据库显示的最新文本有何不同。

words.zhGloss: 尚未编入法规文本的变动
words.enDefinition: Changes already recorded in an editorial system that have not yet been incorporated into the displayed revised text.
acceptedZhAnswers: 尚未编入法规文本的变动

examples.en: The librarian points to outstanding changes to legislation beside the revised text in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂练习中，图书馆员指出修订文本旁标出的「尚未编入法规文本的变动」。

examples.en: We noted outstanding changes to legislation before relying on the online version for our comparison in class.
examples.zh: 在使用在线版本作课堂比较以前，我们先留意「尚未编入法规文本的变动」。

collocations: indication of outstanding changes to legislation

words.enDefinition: In UK legislative databases, a provision shown in the text without having come into force at the displayed point.

examples.en: The website labels the prospective provision separately, and our example asks students to explain that status.
examples.zh: 网站单独标出「尚待生效的条文」，示例要求学生解释这一状态。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which prospective provision was printed but had no commencement date in the displayed text.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，所显示文本中哪项「尚待生效的条文」已经列出但尚无生效日期。

collocations: bring a prospective provision into force
check the status of a prospective provision

words.enDefinition: The opening block of a court document showing how the case is identified, which may include parties and court details.

examples.en: The mock opinion shows the parties and the court in the case caption above the first paragraph.
examples.zh: 模拟裁判意见把当事人与法院的信息放在第一段上方的「案件首部信息栏」里。

examples.en: We checked the case caption to make sure both versions of the fictional opinion concerned the same case.
examples.zh: 我们核对「案件首部信息栏」，确认虚构裁判意见的两个版本指的是同一案件。

collocations: parties listed in the case caption

words.enDefinition: The account of how a case moved through earlier stages or courts before reaching the decision being read.

examples.en: Our case brief summarises the procedural history before explaining the question the fictional appeal raises for decision.
examples.zh: 我们的判例简报先总结「案件程序经过」，再说明这起虚构上诉提出的待决问题。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to extract the procedural history from the opening paragraphs of the sample opinion.
examples.zh: 老师让我们从裁判意见样本开头几段提取「案件程序经过」。

words.zhGloss: 对裁判有实质影响的案情
words.enDefinition: Facts significant to how a court frames or decides a legal issue in a case.
acceptedZhAnswers: 对裁判有实质影响的案情

examples.en: The writing exercise asks students to identify the material facts of a case from the fictional witness accounts.
examples.zh: 写作练习要求学生从虚构证人记述中找出「对裁判有实质影响的案情」。

examples.en: The professor notes that the material facts of a case may differ depending on the issue being discussed.
examples.zh: 教授提醒我们，讨论的问题不同，「对裁判有实质影响的案情」也可能不同。

collocations: identify the material facts of a case
summarise the material facts of a case
compare the material facts of a case

words.enDefinition: The particular question submitted for the court to decide, often stated explicitly in a US case document or brief.

examples.en: The case brief begins with the issue presented before summarising how the fictional court answered the question.
examples.zh: 判例简报先写出「提交法院审理的问题」，再概述虚构法院怎样回答。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether the issue presented is framed more narrowly in the opinion than in the assignment.
examples.zh: 老师询问，裁判意见里「提交法院审理的问题」的表述是否比作业里的更窄。

words.enDefinition: A written statement by a court or judge explaining the legal reasoning or position in a case.

examples.en: The U.S. case reading uses a fictional judicial opinion to show how a court explains its reasoning.
examples.zh: 美国判例读物用虚构的「法院裁判意见」展示法院怎样阐述推理过程。

examples.en: We compared the judicial opinion with the case summary to check which statements came from the court itself.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「法院裁判意见」与案件摘要，核查哪些表述来自法院本身。

words.enDefinition: An opinion whose reasoning is joined by a majority of the judges participating in the decision in question.

examples.en: The fictional court's majority opinion identifies the statutory provision that resolves the dispute about the permit.
examples.zh: 虚构法院的「多数意见」指出了解决许可争议所依据的制定法条款。

examples.en: We read the majority opinion first and then identified the judges who joined it in the mock case.
examples.zh: 在模拟案例中，我们先阅读「多数意见」，再找出赞同该意见的法官。

words.zhGloss: 同意裁判结果的单独意见
words.enDefinition: A separate opinion that agrees with the court's result and may give different or additional reasoning.
acceptedZhAnswers: 同意裁判结果的单独意见

examples.en: The student underlined how the concurring opinion reached the same result using a narrower statutory interpretation.
examples.zh: 学生划出了「同意裁判结果的单独意见」如何通过更窄的法条解释得出相同结果。

examples.en: In the fictional judgment, the concurring opinion agrees with the disposition but gives an additional reason.
examples.zh: 虚构判决中的「同意裁判结果的单独意见」赞同处理结果，并补充了一项理由。

words.enDefinition: A judge's separate opinion disagreeing with the decision or a relevant part of it.

examples.en: The handout lists the dissenting opinion after the majority's reasoning in the fictional constitutional dispute.
examples.zh: 讲义先列出多数法官的论证，再列出虚构宪法争议中的「异议意见」。

examples.en: Our discussion identifies why the dissenting opinion would interpret the two provisions differently in the sample case.
examples.zh: 讨论指出，为什么样本案例中的「异议意见」会对这两项条文作不同解释。

words.enDefinition: In US judicial usage, an opinion supporting the result and joined by the largest group of judges supporting a single rationale, without a majority for that rationale.

examples.en: The casebook uses a fictional split vote to explain why the plurality opinion lacks majority support.
examples.zh: 案例教材用一次虚构的投票分歧解释，为什么「相对多数意见」未获多数支持。

examples.en: We counted each group of judges before identifying the plurality opinion in the American law exercise.
examples.zh: 我们先数清各组法官的人数，再在美国法练习里找出「相对多数意见」。

words.zhGloss: 以法院名义发布的不署名意见
words.enDefinition: An opinion issued in the name of a court without attributing authorship to an individual judge.
acceptedZhAnswers: 以法院名义发布的不署名意见

examples.en: The American courts handout uses a short fictional per curiam opinion to illustrate a different authorship format.
examples.zh: 美国法院制度讲义用一份简短的虚构「以法院名义发布的不署名意见」说明另一种署名形式。

examples.en: We checked whether the sample per curiam opinion named an individual author under the court's heading.
examples.zh: 我们核对样本中的「以法院名义发布的不署名意见」是否在法院抬头下列出个人作者。

words.zhGloss: 法院对法律问题的裁断
words.enDefinition: The court's determination of a legal issue necessary to decide the case, particularly in US case briefing.
acceptedZhAnswers: 法院对法律问题的裁断

examples.en: The American case brief states the holding of the court immediately after setting out the issue presented.
examples.zh: 美国判例简报列出提交审理的问题后，紧接着写明「法院对法律问题的裁断」。

examples.en: We compared the holding of the court with an example the judges mentioned while explaining their reasoning.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「法院对法律问题的裁断」与法官阐释理由时提到的一个例子。

collocations: state the holding of the court
distinguish the holding of the court
scope of the holding of the court

words.enDefinition: The legal reason or principle necessary to the result of a common-law decision, which can have precedential effect.

examples.en: Our common law seminar asks which legal principle forms the ratio decidendi of the fictional appeal.
examples.zh: 普通法研讨课询问，哪项法律原则构成虚构上诉中「判决的必要理由」。

examples.en: The worksheet separates the ratio decidendi from the court's discussion of an issue unnecessary to the result.
examples.zh: 练习单把「判决的必要理由」和法院对不影响结果之问题的讨论分开。

words.enDefinition: A judicial remark or observation that is not necessary to decide the case, though it may have persuasive value.

examples.en: The tutor identifies an obiter dictum in the fictional opinion and asks why it was unnecessary.
examples.zh: 老师在虚构意见中指出一处「判决附带意见」，问它为何对裁判结果并非必要。

examples.en: Our comparison treats the judge's example as an obiter dictum because the issue never arose on these facts.
examples.zh: 在对比中，我们把法官举的例子视为「判决附带意见」，因为案情并未引出该问题。

collocations: treat a statement as an obiter dictum

words.enDefinition: The court's formal ruling about what happens to the case, such as affirming or setting aside an earlier decision.

examples.en: The closing paragraph states the disposition of the case after giving the fictional court's reasons for its conclusion.
examples.zh: 最后一段在给出虚构法院得出结论的理由后，写明「案件的处理结果」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks students to record the disposition of the case separately from the legal test applied.
examples.zh: 练习单要求学生分别记录「案件的处理结果」和法院适用的法律判断标准。

collocations: state the disposition of the case
read the disposition of the case
explain the disposition of the case

words.enDefinition: A brief summary preceding a reported case, typically prepared for publication to highlight its facts or legal points.

examples.en: The librarian shows students where the case headnote ends and the fictional judge's own text begins.
examples.zh: 图书馆员向学生展示「判例提要」何处结束、虚构法官本人的文字又从何处开始。

examples.en: We checked the case headnote against the opinion before quoting either text in our reading exercise.
examples.zh: 在阅读练习中引用任何一段文字以前，我们先把「判例提要」与裁判意见核对。

collocations: verify a case headnote against the judgment

words.zhGloss: 美国判决意见的官方案情与裁断摘要
words.enDefinition: In US Supreme Court publication, the Reporter of Decisions' summary accompanying an opinion for the reader's convenience.
acceptedZhAnswers: 美国判决意见的官方案情与裁断摘要

examples.en: The American court guide identifies who prepares the syllabus of an opinion for publication alongside the decision.
examples.zh: 美国法院指南说明由谁撰写「美国判决意见的官方案情与裁断摘要」，与裁判一同公布。

examples.en: Our class compared the syllabus of an opinion with the court's actual reasoning in a fictional example.
examples.zh: 全班在虚构示例中比较了「美国判决意见的官方案情与裁断摘要」与法院的实际论证。

collocations: consult the syllabus of an opinion
compare the syllabus of an opinion
summary in the syllabus of an opinion

words.enDefinition: A summary released for the public or press alongside a judgment, separate from the court's authoritative reasons.

examples.en: The UK court handout supplies a press summary of a judgment and the full reasons in separate documents.
examples.zh: 英国法院讲义把「判决新闻摘要」和完整判决理由分别放在两份文件里。

examples.en: Our tutorial asks which sentence appears only in the press summary of a judgment of the fictional dispute.
examples.zh: 辅导课询问，哪一句只出现在这场虚构争议的「判决新闻摘要」里。

collocations: publish a press summary of a judgment
consult a press summary of a judgment
compare a press summary of a judgment

words.zhGloss: 独立于报告刊物的中立引证
words.enDefinition: A court-assigned citation identifying a judgment without reference to a particular series of law reports.
acceptedZhAnswers: 独立于报告刊物的中立引证

examples.en: The UK research exercise gives a neutral citation and asks students to find the corresponding fictional judgment.
examples.zh: 英国法律检索练习给出一个「独立于报告刊物的中立引证」，让学生找出相应的虚构判决。

examples.en: The librarian explains why the same neutral citation appears on the court website and in another database.
examples.zh: 图书馆员解释，为什么法院网站与另一个数据库使用同一个「独立于报告刊物的中立引证」。

words.enDefinition: A reference identifying where a reported case appears in a series of law reports.

examples.en: We read the law report citation to find the report series and opening page of the assigned case.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「判例汇编引证」，查找指定判例所在的汇编系列及起始页。

examples.en: The worksheet lists the law report citation separately from the court's own reference for the case.
examples.zh: 练习单把「判例汇编引证」与法院为案件编定的编号分开列出。

collocations: components of a law report citation

words.enDefinition: A citation specifying the exact page, paragraph, or other location relevant to a quoted or supported legal proposition.

examples.en: The tutor asks for a pinpoint citation to the paragraph where the fictional court explains its conclusion.
examples.zh: 老师要求给出「精确页码或段号引证」，指向虚构法院解释结论的那一段。

examples.en: We added a pinpoint citation after checking which page contained the reasoning used in our classroom brief.
examples.zh: 我们核对课堂简报所用理由所在的页码后，添加了「精确页码或段号引证」。

words.enDefinition: An additional citation to the same decision in another source, typically another report series.

examples.en: The sample American citation includes a parallel citation so students can locate the same decision in another reporter.
examples.zh: 美国判例引证样本附有「同案并列引证」，方便学生在另一汇编中查到同一裁判。

examples.en: We placed the parallel citation beside the official citation on the reference card for the fictional case.
examples.zh: 我们在虚构判例的参考卡上，把「同案并列引证」放在官方引证旁边。

words.enDefinition: An authorised publication of judicial decisions, often arranged in numbered volumes.

examples.en: The American law library guide identifies the official reporter used for opinions from the court discussed in class.
examples.zh: 美国法图书馆指南指出，课堂所讨论法院的意见收录在哪种「官方判例汇编」中。

examples.en: The tutor compared an official reporter with a commercial publication containing the same text of the fictional decision.
examples.zh: 老师比较了「官方判例汇编」和一本收有同一虚构裁判正文的商业出版物。

words.enDefinition: The official series publishing opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States.

examples.en: The American research exercise places United States Reports alongside other sources where the same opinions can appear.
examples.zh: 美国法律检索练习把「《美国最高法院判例汇编》」与也可能刊载相同意见的其他来源并列。

examples.en: We used the United States Reports reference to identify the volume and first page on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们根据练习单中的「《美国最高法院判例汇编》」引证，找出了卷号和起始页。

words.enDefinition: A separately issued version of a court opinion released before publication in a permanent volume of reports.

examples.en: The Supreme Court research guide lists a slip opinion before the later printed versions of the same decision.
examples.zh: 最高法院法律检索指南把「判决意见初刊本」排在同一裁判的较晚印刷版本之前。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which citations might change between the slip opinion and the final bound version.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，对照「判决意见初刊本」和最后的合订本，哪些引证可能发生变化。

words.enDefinition: An installment of judicial decisions issued before their appearance in the permanent bound report volumes.

examples.en: The US legal research class compares an advance sheet with a later bound volume of the same reporter.
examples.zh: 美国法律检索课把「判例汇编预印分册」与同一汇编后来出版的合订本相比较。

examples.en: We identified the advance sheet using the publication details printed on the sample cover in class.
examples.zh: 我们根据课堂样本封面上印出的出版信息辨认出「判例汇编预印分册」。

words.enDefinition: A judgment delivered after the court has taken time following the hearing to consider its decision.

examples.en: The mock court schedule shows a reserved judgment listed for release several weeks after the fictional hearing.
examples.zh: 模拟法院日程显示，一份「庭后另行作出的判决」定于虚构庭审结束数周后公布。

examples.en: The English seminar contrasts a reserved judgment with one delivered orally at the hearing in the sample.
examples.zh: 英格兰法研讨课比较「庭后另行作出的判决」和示例中当庭口头宣布的判决。

words.enDefinition: To formally deliver or release a judgment, especially in UK court usage.

examples.en: The UK court schedule shows when judges would hand down a judgment in the fictional case.
examples.zh: 英国法院日程显示，法官何时将在虚构案件中「正式宣布判决」。

examples.en: The news exercise asks whether the court will hand down a judgment immediately after hearing arguments.
examples.zh: 新闻练习询问，法院听完论辩后是否会立即「正式宣布判决」。

collocations: hand down a judgment in open court
date to hand down a judgment
scheduled to hand down a judgment

words.enDefinition: A paragraph identified by a number in a document, facilitating precise references in a judgment or other legal text.

examples.en: The class followed the citation to a numbered paragraph in the middle of the fictional court opinion.
examples.zh: 全班根据引证找到虚构法院意见中部的一处「编号段落」。

examples.en: The online case file keeps the same numbered paragraph even when the line breaks differ between copies.
examples.zh: 即使不同副本的换行位置不同，在线案例档案仍保留同一个「编号段落」及其段号。

words.enDefinition: A searchable collection or service containing court decisions and associated information.

examples.en: The librarian demonstrates a case law database using sample records before students read the assigned judgment.
examples.zh: 在学生阅读指定判决以前，图书馆员用样本记录演示「判例数据库」。

examples.en: Our exercise uses a case law database to distinguish the texts of decisions from summaries about them.
examples.zh: 练习用「判例数据库」区分裁判原文与相关摘要。

collocations: records in a case law database

words.enDefinition: A research tool showing citations to a decision and often how later authorities have treated it.

examples.en: The research tutor uses a case citator to trace which later opinions discuss the fictional earlier decision.
examples.zh: 法律检索老师用「判例引证追踪工具」查看哪些较晚的裁判意见讨论了先前的虚构裁判。

examples.en: Our class checks how a case citator labels later treatment before reading the linked judgments themselves.
examples.zh: 全班先核对「判例引证追踪工具」怎样标注后续处理，再阅读链接所指的判决本身。

words.enDefinition: The later progress of the same case, such as review of the cited decision by another court.

examples.en: Our reference card lists the subsequent history under a separate heading below the citation to the fictional decision.
examples.zh: 课堂参考卡在虚构裁判的引证下，用一个独立标题列出「案件后续程序历史」。

examples.en: We checked subsequent history to see whether the earlier decision was reviewed in the same fictional case.
examples.zh: 我们核对「案件后续程序历史」，看前一裁判在同一个虚构案件中是否受到复审。

words.zhGloss: 后续裁判对先例的处理
words.enDefinition: The way a later court refers to or deals with an earlier authority, such as following or distinguishing it.
acceptedZhAnswers: 后续裁判对先例的处理

examples.en: The research task asks us to compare judicial treatment of a precedent across two fictional appellate decisions.
examples.zh: 检索任务要求我们比较两项虚构上诉裁判中「后续裁判对先例的处理」有何不同。

examples.en: We used the research notes to record judicial treatment of a precedent separately from the original decision's outcome.
examples.zh: 我们用检索笔记分别记录「后续裁判对先例的处理」和原裁判的结果。

collocations: analyse judicial treatment of a precedent
compare judicial treatment of a precedent
track judicial treatment of a precedent

words.enDefinition: The complete text of a judgment rather than a case summary or selected extract.

examples.en: The UK archive exercise asks students to open the full text judgment linked beside the case description.
examples.zh: 英国档案检索练习要求学生打开案件说明旁的「判决全文」链接。

examples.en: Our tutor recommends checking the full text judgment to trace the exact paragraph quoted by the fictional commentator.
examples.zh: 老师建议查阅「判决全文」，找出虚构评论者所引用的具体段落。

collocations: link to the full text judgment

words.enDefinition: A body of legal principles developed through court decisions, in one common use of the term.

examples.en: The introductory reading discusses common law before turning to legislation enacted by the fictional jurisdiction's assembly.
examples.zh: 入门读物先讨论「普通法判例规则体系」，再谈虚构司法辖区议会制定的法律。

examples.en: We identified which principles came from the common law and which were set out in the assigned statute.
examples.zh: 我们辨明哪些原则来自「普通法判例规则体系」，以及哪些原则由指定制定法明确规定。

words.enDefinition: An earlier judicial decision that can provide authority or guidance on a legal issue in a later case.

examples.en: The common law exercise asks which judicial precedent the fictional court uses when explaining the applicable rule.
examples.zh: 普通法练习要求指出，虚构法院阐释适用规则时引用了哪项「司法先例」。

examples.en: Our reading notes identify a judicial precedent cited by both sides in the fictional dispute about local regulations.
examples.zh: 阅读笔记指出，在关于地方法规的虚构争议中，双方共同援引了一项「司法先例」。

words.enDefinition: A precedent that the court must follow on the relevant legal issue under the applicable rules of judicial hierarchy.

examples.en: The seminar diagram indicates which court creates a binding precedent for the court hearing the fictional dispute.
examples.zh: 研讨课示意图标出了，哪个法院能为审理该虚构争议的法院创设「有约束力的先例」。

examples.en: Students ask whether the earlier case is a binding precedent on the precise issue raised in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 学生询问，较早的案例对练习单提出的具体问题是否属于「有约束力的先例」。

collocations: determine whether there is a binding precedent

words.enDefinition: A legal source that a court may consider for its reasoning without being required to follow it.

examples.en: The tutor explains why the fictional judgment treats a decision from another jurisdiction as persuasive authority.
examples.zh: 老师解释，虚构判决为何将另一司法辖区的裁判视为「有说服力的法律依据」。

examples.en: Our model brief cites persuasive authority after checking whether the fictional jurisdiction has decided the same question.
examples.zh: 参考简报先查明虚构司法辖区是否已裁判过同一问题，然后引用「有说服力的法律依据」。

collocations: treat a case as persuasive authority

words.enDefinition: A source containing law or official adjudication itself, such as a constitution, statute, regulation, or judicial decision.

examples.en: The library exercise asks which document counts as primary legal authority for the proposition under discussion.
examples.zh: 图书馆练习询问，哪份材料是所讨论命题的「第一手权威法源」。

examples.en: We marked primary legal authority separately from the legal encyclopedia entry in our classroom research notes.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂检索笔记中，把「第一手权威法源」与法律百科条目分开标记。

collocations: support a proposition with primary legal authority

words.enDefinition: A work that describes, explains, or analyses the law, such as a textbook or scholarly article.

examples.en: The librarian uses a secondary legal source to introduce the terms appearing in the fictional statute.
examples.zh: 图书馆员用一份「法律二手资料」介绍虚构制定法中出现的术语。

examples.en: We linked the secondary legal source to the decisions it discusses in the classroom research exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂检索练习中，我们把「法律二手资料」和它讨论的裁判连起来。

collocations: discussion in a secondary legal source

words.enDefinition: The principle requiring courts to follow precedents of higher courts that bind them on the issue concerned.

examples.en: The American courts worksheet uses vertical stare decisis to explain how a lower court treats higher precedent.
examples.zh: 美国法院制度练习单用「纵向遵循先例原则」解释下级法院如何对待上级法院的先例。

examples.en: Our tutor draws two levels on the diagram before introducing vertical stare decisis in the hypothetical system.
examples.zh: 老师先在示意图上画出两级法院，再介绍假设体系中的「纵向遵循先例原则」。

words.enDefinition: The principle governing a court's adherence to its own prior decisions, including when it may depart from them.

examples.en: We discussed horizontal stare decisis when the fictional appellate court reconsidered one of its own earlier decisions.
examples.zh: 虚构上诉法院重新考虑它自己的一项较早裁判时，我们讨论了「横向遵循先例原则」。

examples.en: The classroom note on horizontal stare decisis explains why the issuing court matters to the precedent question.
examples.zh: 课堂关于「横向遵循先例原则」的笔记解释，为什么先例由何法院作出会影响判断。

words.enDefinition: To apply the relevant rule from an earlier judicial decision when deciding a later case.

examples.en: The mock court explains why it must follow a precedent from a higher court in the same system.
examples.zh: 模拟法院解释，为什么它必须「遵循先例」，该先例来自同一体系内的上级法院。

examples.en: Our assignment asks when a court may follow a precedent from another jurisdiction as persuasive authority.
examples.zh: 作业询问，法院什么时候可以「遵循先例」，把另一司法辖区的裁判作为有说服力的依据。

words.enDefinition: To explain why an earlier case does not govern a later one because a material fact or legal issue differs.

examples.en: The fictional court chose to distinguish a precedent because its statutory provision used materially different wording.
examples.zh: 虚构法院选择「区分先例」，因为该先例涉及的制定法条文在措辞上有实质差异。

examples.en: Our tutor asks students to distinguish a precedent by focusing on the legal issue actually decided.
examples.zh: 老师要求学生着眼于法院实际裁断的法律问题来「区分先例」。

collocations: distinguish a precedent on its facts

words.enDefinition: To decide that a legal rule established by an earlier precedent no longer has the authority it previously held.

examples.en: The American casebook asks when a court may overrule a precedent that it previously treated as binding.
examples.zh: 美国案例教材询问，法院什么时候可以「否定先例的规则效力」，即便过去曾认定该先例有约束力。

examples.en: We discussed what changes when judges overrule a precedent in a fictional case involving a different dispute.
examples.zh: 我们讨论法官在涉及另一项虚构争议的案件中「否定先例的规则效力」会带来什么变化。

words.zhGloss: 本法院首次遇到的法律问题
words.enDefinition: A legal question the relevant court or jurisdiction has not decided before.
acceptedZhAnswers: 本法院首次遇到的法律问题

examples.en: The fictional opinion describes a question of first impression arising under a newly enacted local statute.
examples.zh: 虚构裁判意见称，一项新制定的地方法规引出了「本法院首次遇到的法律问题」。

examples.en: Our case brief explains why the dispute raised a question of first impression for that particular court.
examples.zh: 判例简报解释，为什么在该特定法院看来，这项争议引出了「本法院首次遇到的法律问题」。

collocations: present a question of first impression
decide a question of first impression
address a question of first impression

words.enDefinition: A decision by a US appellate court sitting as a full court or other larger formation provided by its rules.

examples.en: The American research exercise compares an en banc decision with the earlier decision of a small judicial panel.
examples.zh: 美国法律检索练习把一项「全席审理裁判」与较早由小规模合议庭作出的裁判相比较。

examples.en: Our notes flag the en banc decision so students can check its place in the circuit's precedents.
examples.zh: 笔记标出「全席审理裁判」，以便学生核查它在该巡回区先例中的地位。

words.enDefinition: A decision issued by a group of judges selected to hear a case on behalf of a court.

examples.en: The American court guide calls the first ruling a panel decision and explains which judges heard it.
examples.zh: 美国法院指南把第一次裁判称为「合议庭裁判」，并说明由哪些法官审理。

examples.en: The exercise asks us to compare the fictional panel decision with the court's later en banc opinion.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们比较虚构「合议庭裁判」和法院后来全席审理作出的意见。

words.zhGloss: 联邦巡回上诉法院之间的分歧
words.enDefinition: A disagreement between US federal courts of appeals on the same question of law.
acceptedZhAnswers: 联邦巡回上诉法院之间的分歧

examples.en: The classroom table shows a circuit split using two fictional appellate decisions about the same federal rule.
examples.zh: 课堂表格用围绕同一联邦规则的两项虚构上诉裁判说明「联邦巡回上诉法院之间的分歧」。

examples.en: Our case brief asks which reading of the statute created the circuit split discussed in the handout.
examples.zh: 判例简报询问，对制定法的哪种理解导致了讲义所讨论的「联邦巡回上诉法院之间的分歧」。

words.enDefinition: Materials generated during the process of making legislation, considered in legal research and sometimes in statutory interpretation.

examples.en: The American statutory interpretation seminar includes legislative history in a section on materials outside the enacted text.
examples.zh: 美国制定法解释研讨课在讨论制定文本之外的材料时，专设一节介绍「立法过程资料」。

examples.en: We reviewed the legislative history folder before discussing which documents our fictional court considered relevant.
examples.zh: 我们先浏览了「立法过程资料」文件夹，再讨论虚构法院认为哪些文件相关。

words.enDefinition: The intended meaning or objective attributed to a legislature when interpreting its enactment.

examples.en: The seminar asks how competing interpretations of legislative intent relate to the words of the fictional statute.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，相互竞争的「立法意图」解读与虚构制定法的措辞如何关联。

examples.en: Our reading exercise underlines where the opinion describes legislative intent before explaining the court's chosen interpretation.
examples.zh: 阅读练习划出了裁判意见在解释法院所选读法前描述「立法意图」的位置。

words.enDefinition: A formal committee report concerning proposed legislation, which may explain the proposal or record the committee's recommendation.

examples.en: The American library exercise asks us to find a legislative committee report associated with the fictional bill.
examples.zh: 美国图书馆练习要求我们找出与虚构议案有关的「立法委员会报告」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the legislative committee report with the statutory text the legislature eventually adopted for class.
examples.zh: 老师把「立法委员会报告」与立法机关最后通过、课堂正在学习的制定法文本作比较。

collocations: language in a legislative committee report

words.enDefinition: An approach that interprets a legal text in light of the purpose of the relevant provision or legislation.

examples.en: The fictional judgment uses purposive interpretation to relate the disputed wording to the statutory scheme as a whole.
examples.zh: 虚构判决运用「目的解释」，把争议措辞放在整个立法制度安排中理解。

examples.en: Our seminar compares purposive interpretation with another reading that focuses on the words in their immediate context.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「目的解释」与侧重措辞紧邻上下文的另一种读法作比较。

words.enDefinition: An interpretation approach from English law that considers the problem the earlier law failed to address and the Act was meant to remedy.

examples.en: The English legal history class uses the mischief rule to ask what gap the fictional statute addressed.
examples.zh: 英格兰法律史课运用「弊端规则」，探讨虚构制定法填补了什么漏洞。

examples.en: Our casebook presents the mischief rule before comparing it with modern approaches to statutory purpose in class.
examples.zh: 案例教材先介绍「弊端规则」，再将其与课堂学习的当代法条目的解释方法相比较。

words.enDefinition: A canon of statutory interpretation that reads a provision in the context of the entire enactment.

examples.en: The American law exercise applies the whole-act rule by reading the disputed section with the rest.
examples.zh: 美国法练习运用「通读整部法令规则」，把争议条文与其他部分对照阅读。

examples.en: Our outline introduces the whole-act rule after showing how two sections of the fictional statute relate.
examples.zh: 提纲先说明虚构制定法的两项条文有什么关联，然后介绍「通读整部法令规则」。

collocations: reasoning based on the whole-act rule

words.enDefinition: In legal interpretation, on the same subject or purpose so that separate enactments may be read together.

examples.en: The American casebook treats two fictional statutes as in pari materia because they address the same subject.
examples.zh: 美国案例教材把两部虚构制定法按「同类法条合并理解」处理，因为它们涉及同一事项。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether the assigned provisions should be read in pari materia despite their different dates.
examples.zh: 老师询问，指定阅读的条文尽管日期不同，是否仍应按「同类法条合并理解」阅读。

words.zhGloss: 明列一项视为排除其他项
words.enDefinition: A canon under which expressly listing one or more items may signal that comparable unlisted items were excluded.
acceptedZhAnswers: 明列一项视为排除其他项

examples.en: The American seminar discusses expressio unius est exclusio alterius while interpreting a short list in a fictional statute.
examples.zh: 美国法研讨课在解释虚构制定法中的一份短列表时，讨论了「明列一项视为排除其他项」。

examples.en: Our class used expressio unius est exclusio alterius to evaluate one possible inference from the list.
examples.zh: 全班运用「明列一项视为排除其他项」，评估从该列表得出的一种可能推论。

collocations: apply expressio unius est exclusio alterius
invoke expressio unius est exclusio alterius
expressio unius est exclusio alterius canon

words.enDefinition: An interpretive starting point that the same language used in related parts of a statute generally has the same meaning.

examples.en: Our fictional opinion cites the presumption of consistent usage when the same phrase appears in two sections.
examples.zh: 虚构裁判意见在两个条文出现相同短语时，援引了「用语一致推定」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks students to examine whether context might overcome the presumption of consistent usage in this example.
examples.zh: 练习单要求学生考察，在本示例中，上下文能否推翻「用语一致推定」。

collocations: apply the presumption of consistent usage
invoke the presumption of consistent usage
overcome the presumption of consistent usage

words.zhGloss: 不同措辞含义有别规则
words.enDefinition: An interpretive canon under which variations in wording within related statutory provisions may suggest a difference in meaning.
acceptedZhAnswers: 不同措辞含义有别规则

examples.en: The class applies the meaningful variation canon to two fictional sections that use different terms for the applicant.
examples.zh: 全班把「不同措辞含义有别规则」用于两项对申请人采用不同称呼的虚构条文。

examples.en: Our exercise asks whether the meaningful variation canon supports a different reading of the later provision.
examples.zh: 练习询问，「不同措辞含义有别规则」是否支持对后一条文的不同理解。

collocations: example of the meaningful variation canon

words.enDefinition: A grammar-based interpretive principle under which a qualifying phrase ordinarily modifies its nearest reasonable antecedent.

examples.en: Our American legal writing tutorial applies the rule of the last antecedent to a fictional statutory sentence.
examples.zh: 美国法律写作辅导课把「就近先行项规则」用于分析一个虚构法条的句子。

examples.en: Students annotate the last item before explaining how the rule of the last antecedent might affect the reading.
examples.zh: 学生先标注最后一项，然后解释「就近先行项规则」可能怎样影响读法。

collocations: apply the rule of the last antecedent
invoke the rule of the last antecedent
limits of the rule of the last antecedent

words.enDefinition: A grammar-based canon under which a modifier may apply to every element in a straightforward parallel series.

examples.en: The class applies the series-qualifier canon to a modifier following three parallel items in the fictional statute.
examples.zh: 全班用「并列项共同修饰规则」分析虚构制定法中三个并列项目之后的修饰语。

examples.en: Our worksheet contrasts the series-qualifier canon with another approach to deciding the scope of a modifying phrase.
examples.zh: 练习单将「并列项共同修饰规则」与另一种确定修饰语范围的方法作比较。

words.enDefinition: A US interpretive principle favouring a plausible construction that avoids serious constitutional doubt when the statute permits it.

examples.en: The American casebook uses constitutional avoidance to explain a court's choice between two plausible statutory readings.
examples.zh: 美国案例教材用「避免宪法疑义原则」解释法院如何在两种合理的法条解读间作选择。

examples.en: The mock opinion discusses constitutional avoidance only after identifying a serious constitutional question in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 模拟意见先在课堂示例中指出一个严肃的宪法问题，随后才讨论「避免宪法疑义原则」。

words.enDefinition: A rule requiring sufficiently clear statutory language before attributing particular legal consequences to an enactment.

examples.en: Our comparative seminar asks why the fictional court invokes a clear statement rule for one interpretive issue.
examples.zh: 比较法研讨课询问，虚构法院为何在某个解释问题上援引「明确表述规则」。

examples.en: We read the disputed wording to identify what the clear statement rule requires in the fictional judgment.
examples.zh: 我们阅读争议措辞，找出虚构判决所述「明确表述规则」有什么要求。

words.enDefinition: An interpretive presumption that legislation does not attach new legal consequences to past events absent sufficiently clear direction.

examples.en: The American example uses the presumption against retroactivity to distinguish two possible applications of the fictional amendment.
examples.zh: 美国法示例用「推定不溯及既往」区分虚构修订案的两种可能适用方式。

examples.en: Our tutor marks the relevant dates before introducing the presumption against retroactivity in the classroom discussion.
examples.zh: 老师先标出相关日期，再在课堂讨论中介绍「推定不溯及既往」。

words.zhGloss: 普通法上的合法性原则
words.enDefinition: In UK statutory interpretation, the principle that legislation is read as preserving fundamental rights unless clear language or necessary implication displaces them.
acceptedZhAnswers: 普通法上的合法性原则

examples.en: The English law handout illustrates the common law principle of legality through a fictional provision about court access.
examples.zh: 英格兰法讲义用一项关于诉诸法院的虚构条文说明「普通法上的合法性原则」。

examples.en: The class asks which words matter to the common law principle of legality in the fictional judgment.
examples.zh: 全班讨论虚构判决中的哪些文字与「普通法上的合法性原则」有关。

collocations: apply the common law principle of legality
invoke the common law principle of legality
explain the common law principle of legality

words.enDefinition: Wording that imposes an obligation rather than merely granting permission, as interpreted in context.

examples.en: Our drafting exercise asks which part of the fictional provision contains mandatory language imposing a duty.
examples.zh: 起草练习询问，虚构条文的哪个部分使用了设定义务的「强制性措辞」。

examples.en: The tutor compares mandatory language with wording that gives the fictional agency a choice under the statute.
examples.zh: 老师比较「强制性措辞」与允许虚构机构依据制定法自行选择的表述。

words.enDefinition: Wording that allows a person or body to act without itself requiring the action, as interpreted in context.

examples.en: The fictional statute uses permissive language when describing an action the agency may choose to take.
examples.zh: 虚构制定法描述机构可选择采取的行动时，使用了「许可性措辞」。

examples.en: We discussed whether permissive language in one section affected our reading of an obligation stated elsewhere.
examples.zh: 我们讨论一个条文里的「许可性措辞」是否影响对其他地方所定义务的理解。

words.enDefinition: A doctrine permitting departure from a literal reading in the limited circumstances where the result would be legally absurd.

examples.en: Our American law lecture discusses the absurdity doctrine in a fictional dispute about contradictory directions in a statute.
examples.zh: 美国法讲座在一宗关于制定法中相互矛盾规定的虚构争议里讨论「避免荒谬结果原则」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks why the fictional court considered the absurdity doctrine before rejecting one suggested reading.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构法院为何在驳回一种提议的读法前考虑了「避免荒谬结果原则」。
